mainTopic: The end of the אלכסנדר מוקדון story and the close of the פרק with praise of תורה, then a new פרק: the כהנים' morning prayers, the קטורת and אברים lotteries, and the start of the קטורת service.
overview: This amud finishes the אגדה about אלכסנדר מוקדון. The women of Africa mock his greed, and he admits he learned sense from them. He then finds a spring that flows from גן עדן. In one version he follows it to the gate and is turned away, but he is given an eyeball that outweighs all his gold and silver. The רבנן explain that a human eye is never satisfied, until it is covered with dust. The גמרא adds a teaching from תנא דבי אליהו about where גיהנם is. The פרק then closes with praise of תורה learning and the הדרן. A new פרק begins with a משנה about the morning prayers of the כהנים in the מקדש. It goes on to describe the lotteries for the קטורת and for bringing the אברים up to the מזבח, what happened to the כהנים who won nothing, and the כף that the קטורת כהן takes.

steps.title: The women mock אלכסנדר's greed
steps.stepSummary: אלכסנדר complains that people do not eat golden bread. The women answer that if he only wanted bread, he had plenty at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do people eat bread of gold? They said to him: But if bread is what you wanted, didn't you have bread to eat in your own place, that you took up and came here?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אלכסנדר protests the golden bread he was served, and the women turn his words back on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The golden bread was a test. If he needed real food, he never had to leave home. So his whole campaign must have been about grabbing wealth, and the women expose that.

phrases.english: Do people eat bread of gold?
But if bread is what you wanted,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה לָךְ בְּאַתְרָךְ נַהֲמָא לְמֵיכַל,
phrases.english: didn't you have bread to eat in your own place,
that you took up and came here?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להו מי אכלי אינשי נהמא דדהבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אלכסנדר and the women of Africa from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who already has bread at home and goes conquering is driven by greed, not need.

steps.title: אלכסנדר admits he learned wisdom from the women
steps.stepSummary: On his way out, אלכסנדר writes on the city gate that he was a fool until the women of Africa taught him sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he left and came back, he wrote on the gate of the city: I, אלכסנדר מוקדון, was a fool until I came to the land of Africa, of the women, and I learned good sense from the women.
steps.whatsHappening: אלכסנדר publicly admits the women were right. He writes his confession on the city gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mighty conqueror, who won with armies, was beaten by a simple point. His pride is humbled, and he puts it in writing for everyone to see.
steps.whatToRemember: The first part of the story ends with אלכסנדר admitting that the pursuit of wealth for its own sake is foolish.

phrases.english: When he left and came back,
he wrote on the gate of the city:
until I came to the land of Africa, of the women,
and I learned good sense from the women.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי נפיק ואתי כתב אבבא דמחוזא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how אלכסנדר reacted to the women's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלכסנדר admits he was a fool and learned wisdom from the women.

steps.title: A fragrant spring from גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: While eating by a spring, אלכסנדר notices his salted fish take on a beautiful smell. He concludes the spring flows from גן עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he took himself and went on, he sat by a certain spring, eating bread. He had salted fish in his hands. While they were being rinsed, a fragrance fell upon them. He said: Learn from this that this spring comes from גן עדן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new episode in אלכסנדר's travels begins. He finds a special spring and figures out where its water comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salted fish normally smell strong. Here, rinsing them in the spring gave them a wonderful smell, so he reasons the water must come from a holy place, גן עדן. This sets up the rest of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of fish (here, salted fish)

phrases.english: When he took himself and went on,
he sat by a certain spring,
He had salted fish in his hands,
that this spring comes from the Garden of Eden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי שקיל ואתי יתיב אההוא מעיינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new episode of אלכסנדר's travels after he leaves the women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fragrance shows that the spring flows from גן עדן.

steps.title: First version: he washed his face
steps.stepSummary: One version says אלכסנדר simply took some of the water and washed his face with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: He took from those waters and washed his face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two versions of what he did next. This is the first, and simpler, version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the episode ends quietly. He uses the special water and moves on, with no trip to גן עדן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one version of how the spring episode ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He washed his face with the water from גן עדן.

steps.title: Second version: refused at the gate of גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: Another version says he followed the spring up to the gate of גן עדן and demanded to come in. He was told that only the righteous may enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: He went up along the whole of it until he reached the entrance of גן עדן. He raised his voice: Open the gate for me! They said to him: "This is the gate of ה׳, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second version. אלכסנדר tries to enter גן עדן and is turned away with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer quotes תהלים, and the rest of that verse says only the righteous may enter. The hint is that a greedy conqueror does not qualify.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He went up along the whole of it
until he reached the entrance of the Garden of Eden.
"This is the gate of the Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 118:20. The verse ends: "the righteous shall enter into it."

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי אידלי כוליה עד דמטא לפתחא דגן עדן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version, different from the face-washing version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the righteous may enter גן עדן.

steps.title: אלכסנדר gets an eyeball that outweighs his treasure
steps.stepSummary: אלכסנדר insists he is an important king and asks for something. He is given an eyeball, and all his gold and silver cannot balance it on a scale.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too am a king, I am truly important; give me something. They gave him one eyeball. He brought it and weighed all his gold and silver against it, and it did not balance it.
steps.whatsHappening: Turned away, אלכסנדר asks for a gift. The gift is a strange one: an eyeball heavier than all his wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He thinks being a king makes him worthy. The gift he gets is a quiet lesson about his own endless greed, though he does not understand it yet. This sets up his question to the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: תַּקְלֵיהּ לְכוּלֵּיהּ דַּהֲבָא וְכַסְפָּא דִּידֵיהּ בַּהֲדַיהּ,
phrases.english: and weighed all his gold and silver against it,
and it did not balance it.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להון אנא נמי מלכא אנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the second version after he is refused entry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single eyeball outweighs all of אלכסנדר's gold and silver.

steps.title: אלכסנדר asks the רבנן to explain
steps.stepSummary: Puzzled, אלכסנדר asks the רבנן what this eyeball is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to the רבנן: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: אלכסנדר asks the רבנן to explain the strange eyeball. This line sets up their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing he owns can balance the eyeball, and he cannot make sense of it. He turns to the רבנן for the meaning.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the eyeball outweighing his treasure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does this eyeball weigh more than all his gold and silver?

steps.title: The eye of a person is never satisfied
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that this is a human eye, which is never satisfied. That is why nothing can balance it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: It is the eyeball of flesh and blood, which is never satisfied.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן answer his question. A human eye always wants more, so no amount of wealth can ever be enough for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weight stands for human desire. However much you put on the other side of the scale, the eye still wants more. This is exactly אלכסנדר's own problem.

keyTerms.meaning: flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.english: It is the eyeball of flesh and blood,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אלכסנדר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a human eye, which is never satisfied, so no wealth can balance it.

steps.title: אלכסנדר asks for proof
steps.stepSummary: אלכסנדר asks how they know this explanation is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: From where do we know that this is so?
steps.whatsHappening: אלכסנדר is not convinced yet and asks for proof. This sets up the test that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their explanation sounds like a lesson about life, not something you can measure. He wants something he can actually see.

keyTerms.meaning: from where? how do we know?

phrases.english: From where do we know that this is so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer that the רבנן just gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the eye is heavy because it is never satisfied.

steps.title: Covering the eye with dust proves it
steps.stepSummary: Covering the eye with a little dust makes it balance right away. A פסוק in משלי confirms the lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take a little dust and cover it. Immediately it balanced, as it is written: "The netherworld and destruction are never satisfied, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן prove their point with a test. Once the eye is covered with dust, it stops outweighing everything. They back this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dust stands for the grave. Only when a person dies and is covered with earth does his eye finally stop wanting. The פסוק in משלי compares the grave, which is never full, to the human eye.
steps.whatToRemember: The story's lesson: a human eye always wants more, and nothing satisfies it until the person is buried in the dust. אלכסנדר's endless conquests are the clearest example.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a story with a moral (אגדה), not a halachic ruling. Read the eyeball and the scale as a picture of human greed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the whole אלכסנדר story together. Both the women's golden bread and the eyeball teach that chasing more wealth never satisfies.

phrases.english: Take a little dust and cover it;
"The netherworld and destruction are never satisfied, etc."
phrases.notes: משלי 27:20. The verse ends: "so the eyes of man are never satisfied."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof that אלכסנדר asked for.
steps.raayaObject: That the eye is heavy because it is never satisfied.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dust test, together with the פסוק in משלי 27:20.

steps.title: Where is גיהנם located
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו teaches that גיהנם is above the רקיע. Others say it is behind the הרי חושך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of אליהו taught: גיהנם is above the sky. Some say it is behind the Mountains of Darkness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching about where גיהנם is. This teaching connects back to the places mentioned in the אלכסנדר stories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two opinions are given about where גיהנם is. The first places it above the רקיע. The יש אומרים place it beyond the הרי חושך. No proof is given; this is simply a reported tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment for the wicked
Some say: introduces a second opinion

phrases.english: and some say it is behind the Mountains of Darkness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related tradition after the אלכסנדר narrative.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיהנם is above the רקיע. Some say it is behind the הרי חושך.

steps.title: The שכינה is opposite one who learns at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that whoever learns תורה at night has the שכינה facing him. He brings a פסוק from איכה as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Whoever learns תורה at night, the שכינה is opposite him. As the פסוק says: 'Arise, cry out at night... pour out your heart like water before the face of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק begins to close with words of praise for learning תורה. רבי חייא says the שכינה faces someone who learns at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about crying out 'at night' and pouring out one's heart 'before the face of ה׳'. רבי חייא reads it this way: the one who rises at night to learn stands directly before the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who busies himself with תורה learning
The watches, or sections, of the night

phrases.english: Anyone who busies himself with Torah at night,
the Divine Presence is opposite him,
"Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁפְכִי כַמַּיִם לִבֵּךְ נֹכַח פְּנֵי ה׳ (וְגוֹ׳)״.
phrases.english: pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord (etc.)."
phrases.notes: וגו׳ means 'and so on.' Some versions leave this word out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the closing praise of תורה at the end of the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learns תורה at night has the שכינה facing him.

steps.title: תלמידי חכמים bring peace to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה teaches that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world. He proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: Torah scholars increase peace in the world. As the פסוק says: 'And all your children will be taught by ה׳, and great will be the peace of your children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the פרק with one more praise of תורה learning. תלמידי חכמים spread peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins two ideas: children 'taught by ה׳' and 'great peace'. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns from this that people who learn תורה are the ones who bring peace into the world.
steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends on a positive note: learning תורה brings you close to the שכינה and brings peace to the world.

phrases.english: Torah scholars increase peace in the world,
"And all your children shall be taught of the Lord,
and great shall be the peace of your children."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second closing praise of תורה learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק לא היו כופתין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק called לא היו כופתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק לא היו כופתין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not a teaching. It is a closing formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. The פרק is named after its first words, לא היו כופתין.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a פרק
Binding: from the first words of the פרק

phrases.notes: This is the name of the פרק, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final praises.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק לא היו כופתין is complete.

steps.title: The כהנים say a ברכה, the עשרת הדברות, and שמע
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. The ממונה tells the כהנים to say one ברכה. They then read the עשרת הדברות and the three paragraphs of שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The appointed כהן said to them: Say one ברכה! And they said it. Then they read the עשרת הדברות, 'שמע', 'והיה אם שמוע', and 'ויאמר'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It describes the prayer the כהנים said in the מקדש in the middle of the morning עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממונה tells the כהנים to say a single ברכה, and they follow his instruction. Then they read the עשרת הדברות together with the three regular paragraphs of קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of שמע, made up of three paragraphs

steps.confusionAlert: The single word ״וַיֹּאמֶר״ is not a new section. It is the name of the third paragraph of שמע, the one about ציצית.

phrases.english: The appointed one said to them:

phrases.notes: These are the three paragraphs of שמע: דברים 6:4–9, דברים 11:13–21, and במדבר 15:37–41.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם הַמְמוּנֶּה: בָּרְכוּ בְּרָכָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש, the כהנים said one ברכה at the ממונה's instruction. Then they read the עשרת הדברות and the three paragraphs of שמע.

steps.title: Three blessings, plus an extra one on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים recite three ברכות: אמת ויציב, עבודה and ברכת כהנים. On שבת the outgoing משמר adds one more ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They blessed the people with three blessings: אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים. On שבת they add one more blessing for the משמר that is leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the morning prayer in the לשכת הגזית from step 15. After שמע, the כהנים recite three ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 listed one ברכה, then עשרת הדברות and שמע. Now the משנה adds what came after שמע: אמת ויציב, the ברכה about the עבודה, and ברכת כהנים. On שבת the outgoing משמר hands the service over to the next משמר, and the outgoing משמר says one extra ברכה, blessing the משמר that is coming in.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה said right after קריאת שמע in the morning
The ברכה asking ה' to accept the service (like רצה in שמונה עשרה)
The outgoing priestly watch, whose week of service ends on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The morning prayer of the כהנים: one ברכה, עשרת הדברות, three פרשיות of שמע, then אמת ויציב, עבודה and ברכת כהנים, plus an extra ברכה on שבת.

phrases.english: They blessed the people with three blessings:

phrases.notes: This is the ברכה we still say right after שמע in שחרית.

phrases.english: and Avodah, and the Priestly Blessing.
And on Shabbat they add one blessing

phrases.notes: The outgoing watch says this extra ברכה, blessing the watch that is coming in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same משנה begun in step 15 by listing the ברכות said after שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שמע the כהנים recite אמת ויציב, עבודה and ברכת כהנים; on שבת the outgoing משמר adds an extra ברכה.

steps.title: The lottery for the incense, only for newcomers
steps.stepSummary: The ממונה calls only the כהנים who have never offered the קטורת to join the lottery for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Whoever has never offered the קטורת, come and join the lottery. Whoever won, won.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The ממונה runs the third lottery of the morning, for burning the קטורת, and only first-timers may join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most lotteries were open to all כהנים, but this one is limited to חדשים, those who have never done it. The גמרא in יומא explains that the קטורת brings a blessing of wealth, so each כהן should get a turn. "Whoever won, won" means the result is final and that כהן gets the job.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned on the golden מזבח
New ones: כהנים who have never offered the קטורת
Join the lottery (from פַּיִס, a lottery)

steps.confusionAlert: חדשים does not mean new כהנים in general. It means כהנים who have never offered the קטורת before.

phrases.notes: The letter ב marks the next משנה. "He" is the ממונה, the officer in charge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: חֲדָשִׁים לִקְטֹרֶת בּוֹאוּ וְהָפִיסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the prayers end, the משנה moves on to the third lottery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only כהנים who have never offered the קטורת may join the lottery for it.

steps.title: The lottery for bringing the limbs up to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The ממונה calls everyone, newcomers and veterans together, to the fourth lottery: bringing the אברים from the כבש up to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: New and old together, come and join the lottery for who brings the limbs up from the ramp to the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ממונה runs the fourth lottery, and this time everyone may join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the morning the אברים of the תמיד were placed on the lower half of the כבש. Now someone has to carry them up and put them on the מזבח. Unlike the קטורת lottery, this one is not limited, so חדשים and ישנים join together.

keyTerms.meaning: Old ones: כהנים who have already offered the קטורת
The limbs (pieces) of the תמיד offering
The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: He said to them: New ones together with old ones,
for who brings up the limbs
from the ramp to the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: חֲדָשִׁים עִם יְשָׁנִים, בּוֹאוּ וְהָפִיסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next lottery right after the קטורת lottery, but this one is open to all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fourth lottery, open to all כהנים, decides who brings the אברים from the כבש onto the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: no separate lottery is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the כהן who carried the אברים to the כבש is the same one who brings them onto the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The one who brought the limbs to the ramp is the one who brings them up onto the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with the fourth lottery described in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that a new lottery picks who brings the אברים up to the מזבח. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that the job stays with whoever carried them to the כבש earlier, so this lottery is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: The one who brings the limbs up to the ramp,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מַעֲלֶה אוֹתָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: he brings them up onto the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's fourth lottery in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן who brought the אברים to the כבש also brings them onto the מזבח, with no new lottery.

steps.title: The כהנים who did not win are undressed
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים who did not win are handed to the חזנים, who take off their priestly garments except the מכנסים. The garments were stored in labeled compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: They handed them over to the attendants, who took off their garments and left only their trousers on them. There were compartments there, and on each was written which garment it held.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה tells what happened to the כהנים who joined the lotteries but did not win any job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These כהנים had worn the priestly garments in case they won. Now the חזנים take the garments off, leaving the מכנסים so the כהן stays covered. The garments go into compartments labeled for each type of garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Attendants who helped run the Temple

phrases.english: [Mishnah 3] They handed them over to the attendants,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the כהנים who didn't win a lottery and were still wearing the priestly garments.

phrases.english: they would undress them of their garments,
and they would not leave on them
and written on them was the use of the garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the lotteries, deals with the כהנים who won nothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who did not win are undressed by the חזנים down to the מכנסים, and the garments are stored in labeled compartments.

steps.title: The קטורת כהן takes the כף
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who won the קטורת takes the כף, a large gold vessel holding three קבין, with the בזך inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who won the קטורת would take the spoon. The spoon looked like a large gold vessel holding three קבין, and the small dish was inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins the קטורת service by describing the vessel the winning כהן picks up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה returns to the winner of the lottery from step 17. It describes the כף as a big gold vessel holding three קבין, with a smaller dish, the בזך, sitting inside it. This sets up the next part of the קטורת service.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessel (literally "spoon") used to carry the קטורת
A large vessel holding a set amount
Plural of קַב, a measure of volume
A small dish that sat inside the כף

phrases.english: [Mishnah 4] The one who won the incense

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכַּף דּוֹמֶה לְתַרְקַב גָּדוֹל שֶׁל זָהָב
phrases.english: and the spoon was like a large gold vessel
and the small dish was inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בַּקְּטֹרֶת הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶת הַכַּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the winner of the קטורת lottery from step 17 and begins his service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת כהן takes the כף, a three-קב gold vessel with the בזך inside.
